0.comment: Mika: Huffman and the Schmidt Family
0.content: Mika is the second son of the Schmidt family, a household of knights and travellers. His mother writes about local places and conditions; his father is a retired Knight of Favonius; his older brother Huffman is a serving knight who conducts safety patrols. When their parents went abroad, Huffman was meant to raise Mika, but he spent his days at work and his nights drinking with friends, so little Mika learned to look after himself and his brother. Their parents wrote home every week, and Mika traced their routes on a map. That is where his love of maps began. Huffman later told him the family map was outdated, taught him to fight, and joined their father in encouraging him to apply for the expedition: "You don't have to ask too much of yourself."

1.comment: Mika: Eula and the Reconnaissance Company
1.content: The Reconnaissance Company scouts ahead of the Knights' main force, and Mika is its Front-Line Land Surveyor. Its captain, Eula, gave him far more tasks than the other recruits, which quickly made him adaptable. Once he got used to the way she expresses herself, they worked well together. He admires her mental strength: if people stared and whispered at him the way they do at her, he says, he could not leave his room. Eula expected him to last a few days like his predecessors. Instead he did everything without complaint and even volunteered to run her errands and help with communication, which led some knights to treat him as the leaders' official messenger.

2.content: Varka noticed Mika's teamwork during the recruitment trial and took him personally on the expedition as Front-Line Surveyor. He taught him combat every week, set him "homework", and advised him to avoid close combat and use a polearm with a crossbow. Mika calls him a strong leader who commands respect. Jean says Varka chose him less for his qualifications than for his hardworking, grounded nature. Varka jokes that since a lost man needs a mentor and a lost army needs a map, Mika is his mentor; Mika went pale at the joke.

3.comment: Mika: Il Capitano and the Expedition Stand-off
3.content: Deep in a dangerous restricted area in the north, the expedition's vanguard clashed with Fatui scouts, and both sides called for reinforcements until the commanders arrived. At night Mika saw a silent line of Fatui soldiers and, at their centre, a dark figure with glowing deep-blue eyes: the Harbinger Il Capitano. Mika knew he could not survive one half-hearted swing from him. Varka walked out to meet him, they talked briefly, and both forces withdrew. Varka joked that he would have liked a duel, and that the Captain knew a battle in a strange land would hurt both sides.

4.content: Mika's book-shaped surveying device was developed by Mika and Investigation Team technicians using Albedo's latest alchemical components. It holds a notebook with removable pages for making maps quickly. When elemental power is channelled into the carving on its back panel, a prism fires a "wavebeam" at a fan-shaped area. The time the beam takes to return gives the distance, and stronger pulses sketch the local terrain. All the other calculations must be done in the user's head, so only Mika can use it easily. Planned copies for other teams were shelved as spare parts for his. He never boasts about it, partly because that might make more work for Albedo.

5.comment: Mika: Kaeya and the Recruitment Trial
5.content: Because many Schmidts were already knights, the Knights made Mika's recruitment public and raised the bar. Lead examiner Kaeya set the tasks: hiking up Dragonspine in full armour with a heavy load, and mapping a monster-infested region without references. Mika helped the other two successful candidates along the way, treating them as future teammates. Kaeya gave him tips he didn't always understand, and Mika worried he was letting him down. Kaeya's teasing made him so nervous that he wrote Kaeya an apology letter.

6.content: Mika calls Amber the most reliable vanguard. Front-Line Surveyors and Outriders both work ahead of the main force, and she taught him survival skills and how to look after his crossbow strings and arrows. Amber remembers that he answered "Yes, Commander!" to everything because she was close to Eula, and kept calling her "Ma'am" even after she explained she was an Outrider. In 3.1 she told the Traveler his shyness was a roundabout way of showing respect. They defended the walls together in Paralogism (5.6), and she sent the Traveler a message through him to Nod-Krai.

7.content: As a child, Mika studied geography books and practised drawing in the Knights' library. Lisa took a liking to the polite, hard-working boy, recommended books and told him his skills might qualify him for the Akademiya. Through the library he met Ella Musk, who needed a guide for a language-exchange trip into the wilds. On that first real expedition they reached their goal, but a mistake in Ella's word choice got them beaten up by hilichurls. Mika decided he needed to learn to protect himself. Lisa said in 3.1 that if anything were wrong, it would be written all over his face.

8.content: Albedo built Mika's survey equipment; during the Windblume's Breath event (3.5, limited) Sucrose, Albedo's assistant, called Mika an exceptional pathfinder who has taught surveying to others. Mika's attempts at artistic sketches reportedly left Albedo silent for a long time. Klee is Mika's friend and adventure companion. Her explosives keep reshaping the terrain, so he has to redraw his maps, and he thinks it is worth it. She told him about a plant that can relay sound, and he dreams of using it to report terrain from the front.

9.content: Lohen is Vice Captain of the Fifth (Ranged) Company, which splits into squads to back up other companies, and he was a long-time member of Varka's expedition. He is around Mika's age. He checks every survey with Mika and does "armed recon" to fill the gaps, which means charging monster camps alone. Mika started leaving monster gathering points off the maps he handed him; Lohen read the truth on his face anyway. Mika admires his fighting spirit and the way he inspires his companions, but thinks they need teammates to rein them in. He also says Lohen's pranks are "not so bad" once you get used to them.

10.content: In the limited-time Of Ballads and Brews event (3.1), Mika arrived back in Mondstadt carrying a letter from Varka, and Jean had him read it to the assembled Knights. It said the expedition was safe, writing "from the northernmost reaches of Teyvat". It mentioned an unhostile meeting with Il Capitano, who had since been ordered to Natlan, and sent festival wishes, ending with Varka's boast that there are ten captains but only one Grand Master ("His laugh, not mine," Mika added). Afterwards Mika barely managed a greeting to the Traveler before fleeing to report to Eula. Jean said Varka had ordered him back to the Reconnaissance Company.

11.content: In Version 6.0 the Traveler ran into Mika shopping in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. Jean had sent him to deliver the Knights' letters to Varka. He passed on her message that the Knights stand behind their Honorary Knight, gave the Traveler a bottle of cider from Kaeya, and passed along Amber's invitation to come home for Sweet Madame and steak. Varka had asked for Dandelion Wine; Jean told him to travel light, but Mika packed two bottles anyway so Varka wouldn't talk his ear off about it.

12.content: Mika heard about the Honorary Knight when he got back to Mondstadt. He feared that, like many powerful people, they might have a strict code and a temper, and was relieved to find them and Paimon kind. Now he wants to travel with them, survey the land for them and stop "dragging you down". He sends birthday letters with maps and food, suggests code words, and in the Serenitea Pot wants a craggy mountain to keep in shape. His 2026 letter hopes they might meet in Snezhnaya.
